title: Cajun Chicken & Dirty Rice Bowls with Remoulade
displayTitle: Cajun Chicken & Dirty Rice Bowls with Remoulade
seoTitle: Cajun Chicken & Dirty Rice Bowls with Remoulade | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Blackened chicken sliced over Cajun trinity dirty rice with black-eyed peas and a tangy remoulade
subtitle: Blackened chicken sliced over Cajun trinity dirty rice with black-eyed peas and a tangy remoulade
description: Chicken breast gets coated in a bold Cajun blackening rub and seared hard in cast iron—never fried—then sliced over a skillet of Cajun trinity dirty rice with black-eyed peas, finished with a tangy light remoulade and fresh lettuce and tomato.

steps.title: Mix the remoulade
steps.instruction: Whisk mayonnaise, yogurt, Creole mustard, capers, hot sauce, and a pinch of salt until smooth. Refrigerate while everything else cooks so the flavors meld.

steps.title: Season and sear the chicken
steps.instruction: Combine paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, cayenne, and salt; coat chicken breasts evenly. Sear in oil in a hot cast iron skillet 4–5 minutes per side until deeply charred and 165°F at the center. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.

steps.title: Build the dirty rice
steps.instruction: Cook onion, bell pepper, and celery in oil over medium 5–6 minutes until softened. Add garlic and Cajun seasoning, cook 1 minute. Add rice, broth, and black-eyed peas; bring to a boil, cover, and simmer 18–20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.instruction: Portion dirty rice into bowls, top with sliced blackened chicken, shredded lettuce, and diced tomato, and drizzle with remoulade.

proTips: Reduce cayenne by half for a milder version—the smoked paprika still carries plenty of flavor.
Double the remoulade—crews always want extra to drizzle on the bowl.
A dash of hot sauce at the line keeps with the classic po'boy shop presentation.
tonightSpread: Extra hot sauce at the line.
leftovers: Rice, beans, and chicken all keep and reheat together for up to 4 days.
Slice cold chicken over a salad with extra remoulade as a dressing.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Same genuine New Orleans flavor as a po'boy, minus the soggy-bread problem—rice and beans hold and reheat all week instead of going stale on a shelf.
mealPrepNotes: Mix the remoulade ahead—it improves after an hour in the fridge as the flavors meld. Dirty rice and chicken both reheat well together in one container. Station: Vent the hood—blackening in cast iron creates real smoke. Station: Rice and beans hold in a covered pan far better than a sandwich roll ever would—build the bowl instead of rushing to serve it fast. Station: Add lettuce and tomato fresh at serving so they stay crisp.
